sections.h2: Your options for selling in Athens
sections.html:
Athens and Clarke County run as one consolidated government, so assessments, permits and short-term rental rules all come from Athens-Clarke County. You do not juggle a separate city hall and county office. From there you can list with an agent, sell the house yourself, or take a cash offer that skips repairs and open houses.

  • Listing with an agent: a good fit for houses near campus and in established neighborhoods that photograph well.
  • Selling it yourself: practical when you already know what nearby houses have sold for.
  • Cash sale as-is: often chosen for rentals with student tenants, inherited houses and properties that need work.

Whichever way you go, the steps are similar. Pick a price from recent nearby sales, gather the lease if tenants live there, get your latest assessment notice, and choose a closing attorney early. A cash buyer can close on the day you choose because no lender has to approve a loan. Ask for each offer in writing and compare what you would net after costs, not just the headline price.

Athens-Clarke County had 128,612 people in July 2025, up 1.0 percent from 127,357 in 2020. Renters outnumber owners here. Only 40.7 percent of homes are owner-occupied, and about 73 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, a low share that fits a university town. Plan on a buyer pool that includes investors as well as families.

These are countywide middles. A house near campus, a renovated bungalow and a dated ranch on the edge of town will each sit far from them, so ask for recent sales on your own street.

sections.h2: Student demand and the University of Georgia
sections.html:
The University of Georgia is the center of local rental demand, and Athens Technical College, a Piedmont University campus and the Augusta University and UGA medical partnership add more students and staff. For a landlord, that means steady interest in houses within reach of campus.

Pharmaceutical and biotechnology employers such as Boehringer-Ingelheim and Janssen Pharmaceuticals, along with technology firms, also draw workers who rent or buy in town. If you sell a rented house, hand each buyer the lease and its end date early. A sale can close with the tenant in place or after the lease ends.

If your house has been rented by the night, read this before you list. On February 6, 2024, the Mayor and Commission adopted amendments under Title 9 of the county code that define a short-term rental as lodging for transient guests for fewer than 31 consecutive days.

  • Home occupation STRs need an owner-occupant or a long-term tenant of the owner, and only one structure on the parcel can be used.
  • Commercial STRs are not limited that way but go through construction plans review.
  • Hotel-motel tax and a business occupation tax certificate apply, including a 7 percent local excise tax.

Properties on the Legal Non-Conforming STR List, finalized March 1, 2025, can keep operating for up to 24 months from that date. A change in ownership ends the non-conforming status. A buyer who plans to keep renting nightly must meet the ordinance as a new operator. Tell buyers this up front, and ask the Planning Department whether your parcel is on the list.

Georgia's standard homestead exemption is $2,000. Athens-Clarke County goes further: its printed schedule gives $25,000 for the county operating levy and $10,000 for the school operating levy on the regular owner-occupied exemption. Separate codes cover seniors, low-income owners and certain disabled owners.

Both ownership and residence must be in place on January 1, and applications are taken in person at the Tax Commissioner's Office. The cutoff falls 45 days after assessment notices go out, which is usually mid-May. Late applications count for the following year. The county also offers a one-time Homeowners Tax Relief Grant on 2026 bills for owners who qualify.

Moving the house into a trust or adding a new spouse to the deed requires a fresh application, so ask the office before you change title on a house you still occupy.

The clock is 45 days from the date printed on your notice. Phone the assessors first and ask for the appraiser named there. Plenty of disputes get sorted out in that one call.

If the call settles nothing, put it in writing. The county accepts three grounds: value, uniformity or a denied exemption. You can pick the Board of Equalization, arbitration or, for certain properties above $500,000, a hearing officer. Bring recent sales of similar houses and photos of any condition problems. A high bill alone is not a ground.

sections.h2: Hills, weather and what buyers inspect
sections.html:
Athens sits on a string of Piedmont hills. Summers are sticky, winters range from mild to fairly cold, and about 46 inches of precipitation falls in a year. Spring thunderstorms can turn severe. On hilly lots, buyers and inspectors look closely at drainage, grading and roof condition, so repair or document these before showings.

For commuters, the SR 10 Loop forms a perimeter around town, and US 78, US 29, US 129 and US 441 all meet here. Athens Transit is fare-free, which appeals to student renters.

Buyers sort Athens by road and by distance to campus. Broad Street and Atlanta Highway split the city east to west, and Milledge Avenue splits it north to south. Prince Avenue runs through the Normaltown area, where a Piedmont University campus stands.

  • East side: College Station Road, Gaines School Road and Lexington Road (US 78).
  • West side: Epps Bridge Parkway, Alps Road and Timothy Road, meeting the Atlanta Highway corridor.
  • Parks: Sandy Creek Park covers 782 acres around the 260-acre Lake Chapman.

Say which road you are on and which school zone you fall in, in plain words, because both questions tend to come before any talk of price. A one-line note about the walk or drive to campus helps too.

sections.h2: Deed and transfer tax at closing
sections.html:
Before the Clarke County clerk will record your deed, the state's transfer tax has to be paid. It runs $1 on the first $1,000 of price, then 10 cents on every additional $100. By default the seller owes it, but many contracts hand it to the buyer, so read that clause.

The seller's side completes the PT-61 declaration online through the clerks' cooperative authority. Security deeds and certain leases need no PT-61 filing. If you wonder whether an exemption fits your transaction, ask the Clerk of Superior Court for Clarke County. Your closing attorney usually handles the filing and the recording.

faqs.q: Will my Athens house lose its short-term rental status if I sell?
faqs.a: It can. A change in ownership ends legal non-conforming status, so the new owner must comply with the short-term rental ordinance to keep renting nightly.

faqs.q: When is the Athens homestead deadline?
faqs.a: It falls 45 days after assessment notices go out, usually in mid-May. A late application is processed for the following tax year.

faqs.q: Does putting a spouse on my Athens deed affect the homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Yes. Moving the home into a trust or putting a new spouse on the deed requires a fresh application.

faqs.q: Where is the deed recorded for an Athens sale?
faqs.a: The Clarke County superior court clerk records it after the tax is paid and the PT-61 is filed.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Athens student rental with tenants still in it?
faqs.a: Yes. A rented house can sell with the lease still running or once it ends. Review the lease before arranging showings.
